pathways.evidence: glucose is metabolized by these cyanobacteria, using primarily the oxidative pentoses and Calvin pathways (Abstract, p1)
glucose is metabolized by these cyanobacteria, using primarily the oxidative pentoses and Calvin pathways (Abstract, p1)
no proof was found for the involvement of the Entner-Doudoroff pathway in this process (Abstract, p1)

Prochlorococcus and marine Synechococcus strains possess genes encoding the enzymes required to assimilate glucose by using the pentoses phosphate pathway, but not by the glycolysis pathway (Results, p6)
Some enzymes from the Krebs cycle also showed significant increases (Results, p9)
With respect to glycogen metabolism, we observed that the enzyme alpha-1,4-glucan phosphorylase increased in abundance (Results, p8)
We found evidence for fermentation in Prochlorococcus sp. strain SS120 and Synechococcus sp. strain WH8102 after 5 mM glucose addition (Abstract, p1)
Photosynthesis was one of the pathways affected by the availability of glucose in all analyzed strains (Results, p10)
KaiB and KaiC proteins were also affected in Synechococcus sp. WH8102, pointing to a direct link between glucose assimilation and circadian rhythms (Abstract, p1)
the presence of lactate dehydrogenase in Prochlorococcus sp. strain SS120 allows regeneration of NADH, and thus the continuous transformation of glucose into pyruvate. (Results, p17)
